newsitem.title: UK: North Sea wet crude, paper firmer in bullish mood.
newsitem.headline: North Sea wet crude, paper firmer in bullish mood.

text.p: Buoyant demand spurred by short-term bullishness boosted differentials for North Sea physical crude in active business on Friday and paper also traded at stronger numbers, traders said.
The continuing absence of Iraqi barrels and short-term tightness of Atlantic Basin crudes helped hike values for most grades, they said.
Buyers piled into the paper market, with some arguing the end of the OPEC meeting in Vienna made for less volatility on the outright price and meant fair value was easier to assess.
A Gullfaks A loading July 16-18 changed hands at a three-cent premium to Dated Brent, six cents higher than a trade done on Thursday.
An Ekofisk loading July 19-21 moved unchanged at a 20-cent premium to the international benchmark.
A wet Brent was offered at August Brent -15 cents on Thursday -- 10 cents above the last reported trade -- and some traders felt the offer would firm further on Friday.
Swaps firmed sharply. Brent Contracts for Difference for next week traded at August Brent -30 cents, a rise of eight cents. The same was paid for CFDs for July 7-11 and July 14-18.
August Brent was done at $18.07 and $18.06. July/August moved at between -15 and -19 cents, up to five cents stronger.
"It's bullish. The paper market is exploding," one trader said.
In the Mediterranean, Russian Urals sour for loading in the first half of July was assessed 10 cents firmer than the last reported trade at 70-80 cents under Dated Brent.
Values for the second half of the month are less clear, owing to uncertainty over the date of the resumption of Iraqi exports.
